related_questions.question: What is the new treatment for long Covid-19?

text_blocks.snippet: A clinical trial is testing the effects of baricitinib on long COVID symptoms. The REVERSE-LC trial will evaluate the drug's impact on neurocognitive and physical function in patients experiencing long-term COVID-19 effects. Separately, a clinical trial is evaluating AstraZeneca's long-acting monoclonal antibody, sipavibart, for its potential in preventing long COVID, according to Nova Southeastern University.

The REVERSE-LC trial is specifically looking at whether baricitinib can improve symptoms like cognitive dysfunction (thinking and memory problems) and physical impairments that persist for at least six months after a COVID-19 infection. The trial will involve 550 participants aged 18 and older who will be followed for a year. It will also assess the drug's effects on motor control, executive function, memory, exercise capacity, and mental health. The study aims to determine if baricitinib can "turn off the harmful light switch" that alters the immune system in long COVID patients, according to Vanderbilt Health.

In addition to baricitinib, AstraZeneca's sipavibart, a long-acting monoclonal antibody, is also under investigation for its potential to prevent long COVID. This clinical trial is evaluating the effectiveness and safety of sipavibart in preventing COVID-19 and potentially its long-term effects.
